Option A says there's always more water in the morning. I'm not sure about that. I mean, the water level in the reservoirs might vary, but does it always have more water in the morning? I don't think so because it depends on the season and rainfall. So maybe A isn't the right reason.

Option B states that smaller amounts of water evaporate in the cool morning. That makes sense because evaporation is influenced by temperature. Water tends to evaporate more quickly when it's hot. So if you water in the morning when it's cooler, less water might be lost to evaporation. That seems like a good reason to conserve water.

Option C mentions that water used in the morning can be recycled for afternoon use. Hmm, I'm not sure how that works. If you water in the morning, does the water get reused later the same day? I don't think so because once you've used it, it's gone. Unless you have some sort of recycling system, which isn't standard, I don't think this is a common method of conservation.

Option D says grass can absorb water only in the morning. I don't agree with that. Grass can absorb water at any time of the day, as long as the soil isn't too dry. So D doesn't seem correct either.

Putting it all together, B seems to be the most plausible answer because it directly addresses the effect of temperature on water loss through evaporation. This would mean that using less water is necessary because less is wasted.
